tool.name: Convert tabular to Parquet

param.name: header_mode
param.label: Column names
param.option: Datatype default: TSV has a header; tabular has no header
Use the first record as column names

tool.help:
What it does ------------ Converts a tabular file to Parquet format for efficient storage.
The output Parquet file uses default compression setting.
Usage Tips ---------- - By default TSV has a header, while generic tabular retains the first row as data. Override Column names for headerless TSV or tabular files with a header. - Headerless inputs receive names column1, column2, etc. - Header names must be nonempty and unique; inconsistent row widths are rejected. - Empty cells are converted to null/None values in Parquet - Literal NA is preserved, not treated as null. - Entirely numeric columns are inferred as integers or floating-point values when representable. Mixed columns and leading-zero identifiers retain their original text. - Float inference uses ordinary float64 approximation. If a column requires floats, values with magnitude greater than 2^53, nonfinite values, and values that would underflow to zero keep the entire column as text instead. Integer-only columns can still use the full int64 range. - TSV quoting is decoded; generic tabular quotes are literal characters. - Generic tabular comments beginning with # and blank lines are ignored, as in Galaxy. With an explicit first-record header, the first nonblank record is preserved as column names even when it begins with # (for example, #CHROM). - This conversion infers a new schema. It does not restore Parquet types or nested values from a prior text export, and cannot distinguish empty strings from nulls.
